title: B2+ · L19 — Business idioms
description: Idioms del mundo corporativo: move the needle, low-hanging fruit, ROI, boil the ocean, y otros.

questions.prompt: El VP de producto revisa el roadmap del proximo trimestre y quiere descartar iniciativas menores.
questions.question: 'This project will really move the needle' means:
options: Actually move a sewing needle.
Have a significant, measurable impact.
Take a very long time to finish.
Require careful precision work.
questions.explanation: 'Move the needle' = generar impacto medible y visible en una metrica de negocio. Metafora del dial analogico de medidores: solo se mueve con estimulos reales. En cultura corporativa US se usa para descartar vanity metrics ('likes', 'impressions') frente a metricas de fondo (revenue, retention). Error hispano: confundir con 'make a difference' — 'move the needle' es MAS especifico, implica que hay una metrica cuantitativa concreta que sube. Registro: business US puro; en UK se oye pero suena mas americanizado.
examples: Look, we can ship 20 features, but only three of them will actually move the needle on revenue. → priorizacion senior
That's a nice-to-have — it won't move the needle for us this quarter. → descartando iniciativa

questions.prompt: Estas planificando el sprint y quieres arrancar con quick wins para generar momentum.
questions.question: 'Let's start with the low-hanging fruit' means:
options: The smaller trees in the orchard.
The easiest wins that require the least effort.
The fresh produce on sale today.
The most difficult and prestigious tasks.
questions.explanation: 'Low-hanging fruit' = victorias rapidas, baratas, y de bajo riesgo. Metafora agricola: fruta al alcance sin escalera. Estrategia clasica de consultoria: quick wins primero para generar momentum y credibilidad antes de atacar problemas complejos. Cuidado con el registro: si abusas, algunos ejecutivos senior lo perciben como jargon vacio — mejor alternar con 'quick wins' o 'easy wins'. Error hispano: traducir literal 'la fruta baja' — no funciona en espanol, hay que decir 'las victorias faciles'.
examples: Let's grab the low-hanging fruit first — fix the checkout bug, ship the copy update, then tackle the harder architectural stuff. → estrategia de sprint
There's tons of low-hanging fruit in our onboarding flow — we're leaving conversions on the table. → oportunidad detectada

questions.statement: 'Don't boil the ocean' means don't try to solve everything at once — scope down.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Boil the ocean' = intentar abarcar un scope imposiblemente amplio, tipico error de proyectos ambiciosos mal delimitados. Origen: metafora McKinsey/consulting (nunca podras hervir un oceano entero). El consejo 'don't boil the ocean' se ha vuelto refran de gestion de proyectos: mejor un piloto pequeno que un lanzamiento global fallido. Error hispano: no reconocer el idiom y pensar que es literal (climate change). Registro: consultoria y product management principalmente; menos comun en engineering puro.
examples: Great ambition, but let's not boil the ocean — pilot it in one market first and see what breaks. → hedge estrategico
The scope keeps expanding — we're boiling the ocean at this point. Time to cut. → alerta de scope creep

questions.prompt: En el board meeting el CFO presenta una iniciativa y el CEO pregunta por la rentabilidad esperada.
questions.question: 'What's the ROI on this?' asks for:
options: Return on Investment.
Rate of Innovation.
Right of Initiative.
Region of Interest.
questions.explanation: ROI = Return on Investment. Sigla universal en business, pronunciada letra por letra en oral ('R-O-I' /ɑːroʊˈaɪ/), nunca deletreada como palabra. Preguntar 'What's the ROI?' es la forma estandar de exigir justificacion financiera antes de aprobar una inversion. Error hispano tipico: pronunciarlo como palabra ('roy'), suena a novato. Registro: neutro-formal, ubicuo desde startup hasta corporate; en tech se combina con 'payback period' (cuando recuperas la inversion) y 'break-even' (punto de equilibrio).
examples: Before greenlighting the campaign, I want to see the projected ROI over 12 months. → decision de aprobacion
The ROI on employee training programs is notoriously hard to quantify but obvious in retention. → discusion estrategica

questions.text: We need to circle back on the numbers before we can move the needle on Q4 targets.
questions.explanation: Frase 100% ejecutiva. Fenomeno de connected speech: 'circle back on' con /ɔːlbæ/ (elision de la /k/ final de 'back' en habla rapida), sonando /ˈsɜːrkəlbækɒn/. 'Q4' se pronuncia siempre 'Q-four' /kjuːfɔːr/, nunca 'quarter four'. Colocaciones nativas: 'circle back on X' (retomar X mas tarde), 'move the needle on X' (impacto en X). Ambas requieren 'on' — error hispano frecuente: omitir 'on' o usar 'about'.
examples: Let's circle back Friday to see if we're moving the needle on the retention numbers. → seguimiento tipico
We'll circle back on the KPIs at the end of the month and adjust course from there. → planificacion

questions.prompt: Estas en una reunion de 12 personas y surge un tema muy detallado que solo interesa a dos.
questions.question: 'Let's take this offline' in a meeting means:
options: Let's turn off the internet connection.
Let's discuss this separately, outside this meeting.
Let's delete this from the agenda entirely.
Let's print this instead of sharing digitally.
questions.explanation: 'Take it offline' = llevar la discusion fuera de la reunion actual, tipicamente a un 1-a-1 o thread de chat. Idiom fosilizado y algo iranico en la era Zoom: se dice incluso cuando el follow-up sera por Slack (perfectamente online). Uso central en meeting facilitation para respetar el tiempo del grupo. Registro: totalmente naturalizado en US business; en UK se acepta pero suena mas americanizado — alternativa britanica: 'let's discuss this separately' o 'let's pick this up 1-to-1'. Error hispano: interpretarlo literalmente como desconexion.
examples: This is getting really into the weeds — let's take it offline and free up the group. → facilitador cortando el desvio
Happy to dive deeper on that with you — let's take it offline afterwards. → oferta personal educada

questions.prompt: Empareja cada business idiom con su significado en espanol:
questions.explanation: Set esencial de business idioms activo en cualquier call ejecutiva anglosajona. 'Put a pin in it' es sinonimo funcional de 'park it' y 'take it offline'. 'Hit the ground running' se aplica tipicamente a nuevos empleados o proyectos que arrancan con velocidad ya el dia uno. 'Raise the bar' se combina con 'on X' ('raise the bar on quality') — obligatorio 'on', error hispano frecuente omitirlo. Todos neutros US/UK, aunque 'put a pin in it' es mas US.
examples: Let's put a pin in the pricing debate and come back to it after the strategy call. → posponer educadamente
New hires at this company need to hit the ground running from day one — no long ramp-up. → cultura de resultados

questions.target: We need to raise the bar on quality without boiling the ocean — let's focus on the fixes that will actually move the needle.
questions.explanation: Cadena magistral de tres business idioms: 'raise the bar' + 'boil the ocean' + 'move the needle'. Discurso ejecutivo autentico de priorizacion. Ritmo natural: pausa breve tras 'quality', enfasis en 'without', pausa mas larga tras el guion. Contracciones: 'we're', 'let's' obligatorias. Registro: senior leadership, tipico de all-hands o QBR (Quarterly Business Review). Evita sonar a bullshit bingo alternando idioms con lenguaje concreto ('the fixes' — concreto — despues del jargon).
examples: Let's raise the bar on execution this quarter, but keep the scope tight — no boiling the ocean. → discurso de kickoff
We need to move the needle on retention, and honestly, most of the wins are still low-hanging fruit. → discurso estrategico

questions.prompt: En una discusion de arquitectura, un ingeniero senior advierte contra una decision cortoplacista.
questions.question: 'That decision will come back to bite us in the long run' means:
options: Someone will physically bite us later.
It will have serious negative consequences down the line.
It will help us grow in the future.
It will finish sooner than expected.
questions.explanation: 'Come back to bite us' = tener consecuencias negativas que aparecen mas tarde, tipicamente por atajos o decisiones cortoplacistas. Metafora canina/animal muy grafica. Se usa como advertencia estrategica en decisiones controvertidas. Colocacion frecuente en engineering: technical debt 'comes back to bite you'. Alternativa suave: 'bite us in the ass' (informal, en llamadas casuales entre engineers); 'catch up with us' (mas neutro). Error hispano: traducir literal — en espanol seria 'nos pasara factura'.
examples: Cutting QA to hit the deadline is going to come back and bite us in six months, guaranteed. → advertencia de senior
That shortcut in the auth logic will bite us the moment we scale past 10K users. → prediccion tecnica

questions.statement: 'To be in the weeds' means to be stuck in excessive detail and losing the bigger picture.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'In the weeds' = perdido en detalles menores, incapaz de ver el paisaje. Metafora de estar entre matorrales altos sin vision periferica. Consejo comun del manager: 'get out of the weeds' o 'let's zoom out'. Uso doble en restauracion (hospitality US): un camarero 'in the weeds' esta abrumado con pedidos. En business, se usa para pedir subir el nivel de abstraccion. Error hispano: confundir con 'in the woods' (en el bosque, situacion complicada) — significan cosas distintas.
examples: We're way too in the weeds — let's zoom out and remember why we started this project. → llamada al reset
Don't get into the weeds on this call — high-level only, we've got 20 minutes. → instruccion de facilitador

questions.prompt: Cierras una negociacion en la que ambas partes ceden algo y ambas ganan algo.
questions.question: 'It's a win-win' means:
options: Two separate victories in a competition.
Both parties benefit from the outcome.
A children's game or contest.
A losing situation dressed up as victory.
questions.explanation: 'Win-win' = beneficio mutuo, ambas partes ganan. Termino central en negociacion moderna (popularizado por 'Getting to Yes' de Fisher/Ury). Opuestos: 'zero-sum' (una parte gana solo si la otra pierde) y 'lose-lose' (ambas pierden). Uso natural como adjetivo ('a win-win deal') o sustantivo ('it's a win-win'). Error hispano cultural: sospechar del termino como marketing empty — en anglo negotiation se usa sinceramente para estructurar acuerdos duraderos.
examples: Let's structure this so it's genuinely a win-win — otherwise the partnership won't survive year one. → estrategia de largo plazo
You get exclusivity, we get volume — clean win-win. → cierre de negociacion

questions.text: We're behind the eight-ball on this one, so let's get everyone on the same page and pivot quickly.
questions.explanation: Tres idioms de crisis en una sola frase. Fenomeno de connected speech: 'behind the' se reduce a /bɪˈhaɪndðə/ con la /ð/ debilitada en habla rapida. 'Eight-ball' se pronuncia como unidad /ˈeɪtbɔːl/ con leve glottal stop entre 't' y 'b'. 'Behind the eight-ball' viene del billar (bola 8 negra: si esta entre tu bola y el objetivo, estas jodido). 'On the same page' = alineados. 'Pivot' = cambio drastico de direccion, termino startup adoptado en corporate.
examples: We're behind the eight-ball but we can catch up if we align fast and cut scope. → discurso de crisis
Let's get on the same page before we pivot — no point moving in five directions at once. → llamada al alineamiento

questions.prompt: Terminas una call amistosa con un colega de otra area y quieres proponer siguiente contacto sin agendar nada formal.
questions.question: 'Let's touch base next week' means:
options: Let's play baseball together.
Let's have a brief check-in or short catch-up.
Let's travel to a military base.
Let's cancel our arrangements.
questions.explanation: 'Touch base' = ponerse en contacto brevemente, sin agenda estructurada. Metafora del beisbol (tocar la base para no ser eliminado). Uso ubicuo en corporate US, especialmente para follow-ups no urgentes. Registro: neutro-profesional; entre amigos usa 'catch up' (mas calido) o 'ping me' (mas casual/tech). Error hispano: no reconocer el idiom y confundir con instrucciones deportivas. En UK 'touch base' se acepta pero suena mas americanizado — alternativa britanica: 'have a quick catch-up'.
examples: Let's touch base Monday morning to see where we stand on the deliverables. → follow-up estandar
I'll touch base with the sales team and get their read on this before we commit. → recopilando input

questions.statement: 'To be a game-changer' means something that fundamentally alters the situation or industry.
questions.explanation: VERDADERO. 'Game-changer' = algo que cambia radicalmente la dinamica competitiva. Puede referirse a producto, tecnologia, contratacion, o decision estrategica. OJO al abuso: en pitches y marketing se usa TANTO que puede sonar hueco — reservarlo para casos donde el impacto es genuinamente disruptivo. Alternativas mas sofisticadas: 'a paradigm shift' (mas academico), 'a step change' (UK, muy elegante), 'a watershed moment' (formal-literario). Registro: neutro pero desgastado en tech marketing.
examples: This new tool has been a genuine game-changer for our team — we've cut cycle time in half. → uso justificado con dato
The AI feature is a real game-changer for the industry, not just a nice-to-have. → distinguiendo de marketing vacio

questions.target: The launch was a game-changer, but we don't want to rest on our laurels — let's set the bar even higher for next quarter.
questions.explanation: Discurso ejecutivo motivacional que combina 'game-changer', 'rest on laurels' (dormirse en los laureles), y 'set the bar higher'. Formula clasica de kickoff Q2: reconoce el logro + advierte contra complacencia + fija ambicion superior. Ritmo natural: pausas rapidas tras cada coma, enfasis fuerte en 'higher'. Contracciones: 'don't', 'let's' obligatorias. 'Rest on our laurels' viene de la corona de laurel del atleta griego victorioso — metafora clasica que sobrevive en anglo profesional.
examples: It's a huge win — but let's not rest on our laurels. The competition isn't going to slow down. → advertencia motivacional
The bar keeps rising in this industry; complacency isn't an option if we want to stay ahead. → discurso estrategico
